findings.audit_item: Japanese Labor Standards Act Art 37: Night Work Premium (22:00-05:00)
findings.analysis: The code correctly identifies the night work window (22:00-05:00). The test case `13:00-01:00` correctly isolates the night portion (22:00-01:00) for premium calculation. The `PayrollCalculator` applies the 125% rate to night hours.

findings.audit_item: Japanese Labor Standards Act Art 37: Daily Overtime Premium (>8h/day)
findings.analysis: The engine correctly calculates overtime for hours exceeding 8 hours per day. The test case `09:00-21:00` (12 hours) results in 4 hours of overtime, which is subject to the 125% premium.

findings.audit_item: Japanese Labor Standards Act Art 37: Night + Overtime Concurrent Overlap
findings.analysis: The system correctly identifies the intersection of night work and overtime. The test verifies that 180 minutes (3 hours) falling within both categories are paid at 150% (base + 50% extra). This aligns with Art 37, Paragraph 2.

findings.audit_item: Japanese Labor Standards Act Art 37: Break Time Deduction from Night Work
findings.analysis: The test explicitly verifies that a break taken during the night work window (23:00-00:00) is deducted from the night work hours before premium calculation. This prevents paying premiums for non-worked night hours.

The `PayrollCalculator` uses `BigDecimal` with `RoundingMode.HALF_UP`. The statutory rounding test verifies boundary conditions: 324.49 -> 324, 324.50 -> 325. This prevents 1-yen discrepancies in payroll totals.

The `PayrollMapper` uses `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on critical rows (payroll ID, staff/month, store staff). Integration tests verify that concurrent confirmations do not result in double-payment or data corruption.
The `PayrollService` methods are annotated with `@Transactional`. The concurrency integration tests confirm that the isolation level prevents race conditions during monthly payroll confirmation.

The controller validates ownership before accessing payroll data. The dedicated test `StoreAuthorizationServicePayrollOwnershipTest` confirms that a user cannot access another user's payroll (member 42's payroll is denied to member 17).

findings.audit_item: Exception Handling & Boundary Validation: Time Parsing
findings.analysis: The `resolveDateRange` method catches `DateTimeParseException` and converts it to `IllegalArgumentException`. The engine tests verify rejection of clock-out-before-clock-in and out-of-range break times.

findings.audit_item: Exception Handling & Boundary Validation: Negative/Null Inputs
findings.analysis: The rounding logic explicitly handles negative and null inputs, preventing `NullPointerException` or incorrect negative payroll calculations.

findings.audit_item: Data Integrity: UTF-8 Encoding in Demo Data
findings.analysis: The PowerShell script uses stdin redirection to avoid code-page corruption. The evidence confirms that Japanese names are stored correctly in UTF-8 (e.g., `E794B0E4B8AD...`), not as question marks (`0x3F`).
The frontend `calendar.html` now correctly maps the `CalendarEventDto` fields (`id`, `title`, `start`, `end`, `extendedProps`) instead of the raw `ShiftDto`. This resolves the empty calendar issue.
The fetch interceptor correctly prioritizes the `XSRF-TOKEN` cookie for mutation requests. Integration tests verify the CSRF token lifecycle and security enforcement.
The final isolated regression run executed 83 tests with 0 failures and 0 errors. This includes specific tests for payroll ownership, concurrency, and statutory rounding.
The browser UI was verified to display correct payroll data (佐藤 花子 ¥141,700, 鈴木 一郎 ¥164,332). The Excel download was successfully generated and inspected, confirming end-to-end functionality.
